item.title: Ride: Stay present when you shut down (Adam Young Part 2)
item.description: The Place We Find Ourselves ep 80 — Relational Conflict: Fight, Flight, Freeze, or Shut Down Part 2. Adam Young (Allender/Eldredge world) on shutdown vs staying in contact. From The Place We Find Ourselves.

item.itunes:summary: Christian counselor Adam Young names shutdown as going offline and social engagement—staying in contact—as the alternative. For dismissive-avoidant presence and repair.

item.title: Ride: Here but not really — fighting emotional absence

item.itunes:summary: Matt & Sarah Hammitt on being physically home and emotionally gone—and choosing to stay and hear without defending. Presence after shutdown.

item.title: Ride: Build atomic habits with James Clear
item.description: Atomic Habits author James Clear joins Chris Duffy to unpack the science of habit formation, how to work with your motivations, and why stacking small habits beats relying on willpower. From How to Be a Better Human (TED Audio Collective).
item.itunes:title: Ride: Build atomic habits with James Clear
item.itunes:summary: James Clear walks through habit formation, motivation, and why tiny consistent behaviors compound into identity-level change—core Atomic Habits ideas in a car-ride length.
item.itunes:author: Tobias / PretzelerFL / mowgli42

item.title: Ride: Kick the procrastination habit
item.description: Social psychologist Ayelet Fishbach explains the science of motivation and four proven tactics to interrupt the procrastination habit while staying happy and engaged. From TED Talks Daily.
item.itunes:title: Ride: Kick the procrastination habit
item.itunes:summary: Motivation scientist Ayelet Fishbach shares research-backed cognitive tricks to stay engaged and finish what you start—practical anti-procrastination systems.
item.itunes:author: Tobias / PretzelerFL / mowgli42

item.title: Ride: Three habits to escape your phone
item.description: Nayeema Raza describes how screens reshape attention and shares three habits to reignite curiosity, restore presence, and loosen phone addiction—followed by a short host interview. From TED Talks Daily.
item.itunes:title: Ride: Three habits to escape your phone
item.itunes:summary: Journalist Nayeema Raza offers three practical habits to restore curiosity and presence when phone use has become the default system running your day.
item.itunes:author: Tobias / PretzelerFL / mowgli42

item.title: Ride: Power of Habit with Charles Duhigg
item.description: Erik Fisher talks with Charles Duhigg (The Power of Habit; Smarter Faster Better) about habit loops and peak productivity practices for work and life. From Beyond the To-Do List.

item.itunes:summary: Pulitzer winner Charles Duhigg connects The Power of Habit loops to the productivity systems in Smarter Faster Better—cue, routine, reward applied to real work.
item.itunes:author: Tobias / PretzelerFL / mowgli42

item.itunes:title: Ride: Morning routines that actually work
